questions.q: Why should the king of Ammon not occupy the land of Gad?
questions.a: The king of Ammon should not occupy Gad because Israel still has sons and an heir to live in the land.

questions.q: What will happen to Rabbah?
questions.a: It will become a heap of ruins, and the villages around it will be burned with fire.

questions.q: What will happen to the king of the Ammonites and his priests and officials?
questions.a: They will all go into exile together.

questions.q: What do the rebellious people of Ammon trust in?
questions.a: They trust in their treasures.

questions.q: What will happen to the people of Ammon when Yahweh brings terror on them from all around?
questions.a: They will be scattered, and no one will gather the people who flee.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do for the people of Ammon after that?
questions.a: Yahweh will restore their former prosperity.

questions.q: What has happened to the wisdom of the discerning people in Teman, in Edom?
questions.a: Their advice has been lost, and their wisdom has disappeared.

questions.q: What does Yahweh tell the people of Dedan to do?
questions.a: He tells them to flee and to hide in deep caves.

questions.q: What is Yahweh going to do to Esau?
questions.a: He is going to bring disaster on Esau at the time he punishes him.

questions.q: What would grape gatherers leave behind after they harvest grapes?
questions.a: They would leave some grapes behind.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to the hiding places of Esau?
questions.a: He will uncover them, so that Esau will not be able to hide.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say about the fatherless children and widows of Edom?
questions.a: He says that he will keep the fatherless children alive and that the widows should trust in him.

questions.q: Why should the Edomites already know that Yahweh will punish them?
questions.a: Even people who did not deserve to suffer Yahweh’s punishment must suffer it, so the Edomites will not escape punishment.

questions.q: What did Yahweh swear by himself will happen to Bozrah?
questions.a: He swore that Bozrah will become a horror, something people mock, and a for curse, and that all its cities will be ruins forever.

questions.q: What did Yahweh’s messenger tell the nations to do?
questions.a: He told them to gather, get ready for battle, and attack Edom.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say to the people of Edom?
questions.a: He says that he will make Edom unimportant among the nations and that everyone will despise them.

questions.q: Because the Edomites have deceived themselves with their pride and think they are safe in the rocky cliffs, what will Yahweh do to them?
questions.a: He will bring them down from there.

questions.q: To what does Yahweh compare the horror of Edom?
questions.a: He compares it to the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and the towns near them, where no one lives.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do after he drives the Edomites out of their land?
questions.a: He will appoint over Edom the leader he chooses.

questions.q: What are the plans that Yahweh has against Edom?
questions.a: He plans for enemies to drag away even the youngest and weakest people of Teman and to turn their homeland into a wasteland.

questions.q: What will it be like when Edom is destroyed?
questions.a: The earth will shake at the sound of their falling, and people as far away as the Sea of Reeds will hear their cry. The warriors of Edom will be terrified.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say will happen to the people of Damascus?
questions.a: They will become weak, turn to flee, and tremble with fear. They will suffer great distress and pain.

questions.q: What will happen to the famous city that Yahweh was pleased with?
questions.a: It will be abandoned.

questions.q: What will happen when Yahweh lights a fire on the wall of Damascus?
questions.a: The fire will burn up the palaces of Ben Hadad. The young men will fall in the open squares, and all the soldiers will die.

questions.q: What does Yahweh tell the attackers to do to Kedar?
questions.a: He tells them to attack Kedar and destroy the people of the east. They will take the people’s tents, flocks, and camels.

questions.q: Why will it be easy to attack the nation that lives in security?
questions.a: The nation has no doors or bars, and its people live alone.

questions.q: Where does Yahweh tell the people of Hazor to go?
questions.a: He tells them to flee far away and hide in deep caves.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to the people of Hazor when their camels and livestock become plunder?
questions.a: He will scatter them in every direction and bring disaster on them from every side.

questions.q: Who will live in Hazor after it is destroyed?
questions.a: Only jackals will live in Hazor, and no person will live there.

questions.q: When Yahweh destroys the archers of Elam, where will the people go?
questions.a: The people of Elam will be scattered, and the exiles will go to every nation.

questions.q: When did Jeremiah receive the prophecy about Elam?
questions.a: He received it at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah.

questions.q: What is Yahweh going to do because he is angry with the people of Elam?
questions.a: He will make them terrified before their enemies, bring disaster on them, and send the sword after them until he has finished them. He will also set his throne in Elam and destroy its king and officials.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do for the people of Elam in the future?
questions.a: He will restore their former prosperity.

commentary.text: Prophecies relative to the Ammonites. (Jer. 49:1-6) The Edomites. (Jer. 49:7-22) The Syrians. (Jer. 49:23-27) The Kedarenes. (Jer. 49:28-33) The Elamites. (Jer. 49:34-39)

Jer. 49:1-6. Might often prevails against right among men, yet that might shall be controlled by the Almighty, who judges aright; and those will find themselves mistaken, who, like the Ammonites, think every thing their own on which they can lay their hands. The Lord will call men to account for every instance of dishonesty, especially to the destitute.

Jer. 49:7-22 The Edomites were old enemies to the Israel of God. But their day is now at hand; it is foretold, not only to warn them, but for the sake of the Israel of God, whose afflictions were aggravated by them. Thus Divine judgments go round from nation to nation; the earth is full of commotion, and nothing can escape the ministers of Divine vengeance. The righteousness of God is to be observed amidst the violence of men.

Jer. 49:23-27 How easily God can dispirit those nations that have been most celebrated for valour! Damascus waxes feeble. It was a city of joy, having all the delights of the sons of men. But those deceive themselves who place their happiness in carnal joys.

Jer. 49:28-33 Nebuchadnezzar would make desolation among the people of Kedar, who dwelt in the deserts of Arabia. He who conquered many strong cities, will not leave those unconquered that dwell in tents. He will do this to gratify his own covetousness and ambition; but God orders it for correcting an unthankful people, and for warning a careless world to expect trouble when they seem most safe. They shall flee, get far off, and dwell deep in the deserts; they shall be dispersed. But privacy and obscurity are not always protection and security.

Jer. 49:34-39 The Elamites were the Persians; they acted against God's Israel, and must be reckoned with. Evil pursues sinners. God will make them know that he reigns. Yet the destruction of Elam shall not be for ever. But this promise was to have its full accomplishment in the days of the Messiah. In reading the Divine assurance of the destruction of all the enemies of the church, the believer sees that the issue of the holy war is not doubtful. It is blessed to recollect, that He who is for us, is more than all against us. And he will subdue the enemies of our souls.
